key_insight: A new large-deviation framework for local weak wave turbulence captures both typical and rare spectrum fluctuations and reveals long-range correlations beyond classical kinetic theory.
engineering_relevance: The theory gives engineers a practical way to predict finite-size, intermittent, and boundary-driven fluctuations in wave spectra, which is useful for modeling real dispersive wave systems.
method: Derive a large deviation principle specialized to local wave interactions.
Analyze Gaussian fluctuations around out-of-equilibrium spectra.
Decompose long-range correlations into bulk flux and forcing-related contributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations and first-time calculations for fixed-flux boundary conditions, with qualitative and numerical predictions rather than a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: Results rely on asymptotic assumptions and specialized boundary conditions, so direct transfer to strongly nonlinear or nonlocal wave systems may require additional validation.
paper_title: Dynamical large deviations and long-range correlations for local weak wave turbulence
